questions.q: A 25-year-old man presents with well-demarcated, scaly, brownish patches in the groin folds. On Wood's lamp examination, the lesion shows coral-red fluorescence. What is the metabolite responsible for this characteristic fluorescence?
questions.exp: Coral-red fluorescence under Wood's lamp is characteristic of erythrasma caused by Corynebacterium minutissimum, which produces coproporphyrin III. This finding helps differentiate erythrasma from tinea cruris, which does not fluoresce.

questions.q: A 12-year-old boy with cervical lymph node tuberculosis develops asymptomatic, symmetrical crops of dusky red papules on his elbows and knees. The papules show central crusting and heal with pox-like pitted scars. Which histopathological feature is MOST characteristic of this condition?
opts: Diffuse neutrophilic infiltrate with abundant acid-fast bacilli
Wedge-shaped dermal necrosis with palisading histiocytes and vasculitis
Band-like lymphocytic infiltrate obscuring the dermoepidermal junction
questions.exp: The clinical description is consistent with Papulonecrotic Tuberculid (PNT), which presents with papules that undergo central necrosis and heal with varioliform scars. The characteristic histopathology shows epidermal ulceration with an underlying wedge-shaped area of dermal necrosis surrounded by palisading histiocytes and well-formed granulomas, accompanied by leukocytoclastic or granulomatous vasculitis.

questions.q: A 28-year-old man presents with recurrent skin infections caused by Escherichia coli. Skin biopsy and functional studies reveal a deficiency of a specific antimicrobial peptide primarily produced by keratinocytes and sebocytes. Which antimicrobial peptide is most likely deficient in this patient?
questions.exp: Psoriasin (S100A7) is primarily found in keratinocytes and sebocytes and specifically protects human skin from Escherichia coli infection. Its deficiency would predispose to recurrent E. coli skin infections.

questions.q: During nail surgery, a tourniquet is applied to maintain hemostasis. What is the primary reason a bloodless field is essential in nail unit procedures?
opts: To allow clear visualization of the delicate nail matrix and nail bed anatomy
To minimize the need for local anesthesia
questions.exp: A tourniquet provides a bloodless field which is strictly essential for clear visualization of the delicate nail matrix and nail bed anatomy. This allows precise identification of structures and helps prevent inadvertent injury to the matrix.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with pruritic violaceous polygonal papules on her wrists and oral white lacy lesions. A skin biopsy shows a band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at the dermo-epidermal junction with apoptotic keratinocytes. Which cells are characteristically found in close proximity to the damaged basal keratinocytes in this condition?
questions.exp: In lichen planus, CD8+ cytotoxic T-cells are characteristically found in close proximity to damaged basal keratinocytes, while CD4+ T-helper cells predominate in the dermis. This distribution reflects the T-cell mediated attack on basal keratinocytes expressing altered self-antigens.

questions.q: A 38-year-old patient with multibacillary leprosy develops a corneal ulcer in his right eye. He reports no pain or awareness of any injury. Which combination of pathogenic mechanisms best explains this complication?
opts: Direct bacillary invasion of cornea and Type 2 lepra reaction
Facial nerve palsy causing lagophthalmos and trigeminal nerve involvement causing corneal anesthesia
Blocked nasolacrimal duct and scleritis leading to corneal perforation
Posterior segment extension and choroidal inflammation
questions.exp: Corneal ulcers in leprosy are caused by secondary bacterial or fungal infections, not direct M. leprae invasion. The combination of lagophthalmos (from facial nerve palsy) exposing the cornea and corneal anesthesia (from trigeminal nerve involvement) prevents detection of minor trauma, leading to ulcer formation.

questions.q: Which of the following antimicrobial peptides is secreted exclusively by eccrine sweat glands?
questions.exp: Dermcidin (DCD-1) is secreted by eccrine sweat gland epithelial cells and exhibits broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity. In contrast, defensins and cathelicidins are produced by keratinocytes and other cell types, while psoriasin is produced by keratinocytes and sebocytes.

questions.q: A 65-year-old man undergoes cryotherapy for a biopsy-proven superficial basal cell carcinoma on his forehead. Which freezing protocol would provide maximum tissue destruction for this malignant lesion?
opts: Single rapid freeze with rapid thaw
Single slow freeze with slow thaw
Double freeze-thaw cycle with rapid freeze and slow thaw
Double freeze-thaw cycle with slow freeze and rapid thaw
questions.exp: For malignant lesions, a double freeze-thaw cycle is recommended as the first cycle impairs local circulation and increases tissue conductivity, allowing deeper penetration during the second freeze. Additionally, rapid freezing promotes intracellular ice crystal formation while slow thawing maximizes cellular damage through prolonged hypotonic exposure and ice recrystallization.

questions.q: A 3-year-old child presents with recurrent pneumonia (4 episodes in the past year), persistent oral thrush despite treatment, and unusual infection with Pneumocystis jirovecii. Which mnemonic helps identify warning signs for primary immunodeficiency evaluation?
opts: SPUR - Serious, Persistent, Unusual, Recurrent infections
TORCH - Toxoplasma, Other, Rubella, CMV, Herpes
questions.exp: SPUR is a clinical mnemonic used to identify warning signs of primary immunodeficiency: Serious infections requiring hospitalization, Persistent infections not responding to standard treatment, Unusual organisms or sites, and Recurrent infections. This child demonstrates all four features warranting immunological workup.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with a 1.5 cm pigmented lesion on her back with irregular borders and color variegation. Dermoscopy reveals atypical network and blue-white veil. Which biopsy technique is most appropriate?
opts: 4 mm punch biopsy from the darkest area
Incisional biopsy of the thickest portion
questions.exp: Excisional biopsy is the gold standard for suspected melanoma as it provides the entire lesion for accurate Breslow depth measurement. Shave biopsy is contraindicated as it compromises staging, and punch biopsy risks sampling error in heterogeneous lesions.

questions.q: The current prophylactic HPV vaccines (Gardasil, Cervarix) contain virus-like particles (VLPs) that are composed of which viral protein?
questions.exp: Recombinant L1 major capsid proteins can self-assemble into virus-like particles (VLPs) that lack viral DNA but display surface epitopes identical to native virions, inducing robust neutralizing antibody responses. These L1-based VLPs form the basis of current prophylactic HPV vaccines.

questions.q: The fundamental pathogenetic mechanism underlying dermatomyositis differs from polymyositis in that dermatomyositis is primarily characterized by:
opts: CD8+ cytotoxic T-cell mediated myocyte destruction
Natural killer cell infiltration of muscle
questions.exp: Dermatomyositis is fundamentally a humorally mediated microangiopathy, distinct from polymyositis which is driven by CD8+ cytotoxic T-cell-mediated myocyte destruction. This pathogenetic difference is a key distinguishing feature between these two conditions.

questions.q: A 28-year-old male presents with purulent urethral discharge. Gram stain of the discharge shows Gram-negative intracellular diplococci within neutrophils. Culture on Modified Thayer-Martin medium grows oxidase-positive colonies. Carbohydrate utilization test shows acid production from glucose only, with no reaction to maltose, sucrose, or lactose. Which organism is most likely responsible?
questions.exp: Neisseria gonorrhoeae characteristically ferments glucose only and is negative for maltose, sucrose, and lactose. This distinguishes it from N. meningitidis, which ferments both glucose and maltose.

questions.q: A 42-year-old HIV-positive patient on tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF)-based regimen presents with glycosuria, phosphaturia, and aminoaciduria despite normal serum glucose levels. Which complication of TDF therapy does this clinical picture represent?
questions.exp: TDF is uniquely associated with nephrotoxicity and renal tubular dysfunction manifesting as Fanconi syndrome, characterized by proximal tubular dysfunction leading to glycosuria, phosphaturia, and aminoaciduria. Strict renal monitoring is required during TDF therapy.

questions.q: A 45-year-old diabetic woman presents with multiple yellowish papules on her lower eyelids. Biopsy shows ductal structures lined by cells with abundant clear cytoplasm. Which staining characteristic would confirm the nature of the intracellular substance in this clear cell variant?
questions.exp: The clear cell variant of syringoma, which is strongly associated with diabetes mellitus, shows epithelial cells with abundant clear cytoplasm due to massive intracellular glycogen accumulation. Glycogen is characteristically PAS-positive and diastase-labile, meaning the staining disappears after diastase digestion.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman undergoes a nail matrix biopsy for longitudinal melanonychia. Postoperatively, she develops a permanent longitudinal split in her nail plate. Which anatomical structure was most likely injured during the procedure?
questions.exp: The nail matrix (germinal matrix) is the germinative center that produces the nail plate. Injury to this structure causes permanent nail dystrophy including scarring, ridging, or splitting of the nail plate.

questions.q: A 35-year-old HIV-positive man is being initiated on antiretroviral therapy containing abacavir. Before starting the drug, the treating physician orders a specific genetic test. Which allele, if positive, would contraindicate the use of abacavir?
questions.exp: HLA-B*5701 screening is mandatory before initiating abacavir therapy as this allele strongly predicts a potentially fatal hypersensitivity reaction. Symptoms progressively worsen upon re-challenge and can lead to cardiovascular collapse and death.

questions.q: A dark-skinned patient develops permanent depigmentation following cryotherapy for a common wart, despite minimal tissue destruction. Which cellular characteristic best explains this complication?
opts: Melanocytes are destroyed at -4°C to -7°C while keratinocytes require -20°C to -40°C
Fibroblasts in dark skin are more cryosensitive than in fair skin
Keratinocytes release cytotoxic mediators that selectively destroy melanocytes
Melanocytes have higher water content causing greater osmotic damage
questions.exp: Melanocytes are the most cryosensitive cells, undergoing cell death at just -4°C to -7°C, compared to keratinocytes which require -20°C to -40°C for destruction. This differential sensitivity explains why hypopigmentation commonly occurs even with minimal freezing, as melanocytes are destroyed at temperatures that spare other epidermal cells.

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman undergoes cervical biopsy showing high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL). Molecular analysis reveals HPV-16 DNA integration into the host genome. Which mechanism best explains the oncogenic progression following viral integration?
opts: Loss of E1 helicase function preventing viral replication
Disruption of E2 leading to uncontrolled E6/E7 expression
Upregulation of L1 capsid protein synthesis
questions.exp: When HPV integrates into host DNA, the E2 gene is frequently disrupted. Since E2 normally represses transcription of the E6 and E7 oncogenes, its loss leads to uncontrolled expression of these oncoproteins, driving cellular transformation and oncogenesis.

questions.q: Which of the following clinical features in a child would NOT be considered a warning sign for primary immunodeficiency according to the SPUR criteria?
opts: Two pneumonias requiring IV antibiotics in one year
Candidiasis resolving with single course of fluconazole
Mycobacterium avium complex infection in an infant
Eight otitis media episodes in twelve months
questions.exp: Candidiasis that resolves with standard single-course treatment does not meet SPUR criteria as it is neither persistent nor recurrent. SPUR criteria include Serious infections, Persistent infections not clearing with appropriate therapy, Unusual pathogens, and Recurrent infections suggesting underlying immunodeficiency.

questions.q: A clinician suspects gonococcal pharyngitis in a patient and considers diagnostic options. Which statement regarding the diagnosis of Neisseria gonorrhoeae at pharyngeal sites is correct?
opts: Gram stain is highly sensitive and recommended as first-line investigation
Culture is preferred over NAAT due to higher sensitivity at this site
NAAT is recommended due to poor sensitivity of Gram stain and presence of commensal Neisseria species
Oxidase test on pharyngeal swab can definitively confirm gonorrhea
questions.exp: Gram staining is not recommended for pharyngeal specimens due to extremely poor sensitivity and the presence of morphologically similar commensal bacteria. NAAT is the preferred method at extragenital sites due to its superior sensitivity (>95%).

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman presents with recurrent tender nodules on the posterior aspects of both calves. Some lesions have ulcerated, leaving shallow ulcers with bluish undermined borders. She has a BMI of 32 and works as a cashier standing for long hours. Skin biopsy is most likely to show which of the following histopathological findings?
opts: Lobular panniculitis with granulomatous inflammation and vasculitis
Superficial and deep perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate
questions.exp: This clinical presentation is classic for Erythema Induratum of Bazin (EIB), which occurs in young-to-middle-aged women with risk factors like obesity and venous stasis. Histopathologically, EIB is the prototype of predominantly lobular panniculitis associated with granulomatous inflammation, focal necrosis, and vasculitis affecting vessels of various sizes.

questions.q: During closure of a large scalp defect following tumor excision, which undermining plane provides the greatest tissue advancement while minimizing bleeding?
questions.exp: The subgaleal plane is the preferred undermining plane for scalp surgery as it is relatively avascular and allows significant tissue advancement (5 cm undermining yields 2-3 cm advancement). The supraperiosteal plane is reserved for areas over bony prominences.

questions.q: A culture from a chronic onychomycosis patient grows on Sabouraud dextrose agar showing a white fluffy colony with wine-red reverse pigment. Lactophenol cotton blue mount reveals tear-shaped microconidia arranged along the hyphae. Which organism is most likely responsible?
questions.exp: Trichophyton rubrum characteristically produces colonies with a white fluffy surface and cherry-red to wine-red reverse pigment. Microscopically, it shows sparse tear-shaped or peg-shaped microconidia arranged in a 'birds on a fence' pattern along the hyphae.

questions.q: Which of the following represents the earliest innate immune event in the pathogenesis of lichen planus that subsequently leads to T-cell mediated damage?
opts: Release of CXCL9 and CXCL10 by keratinocytes
Production of Type 1 interferons (IFN-α) by plasmacytoid dendritic cells
questions.exp: Plasmacytoid dendritic cells are stimulated via Toll-like receptors and release Type 1 interferons (IFN-α), which represents an early event in the innate immune cascade that precedes and leads to T-cell mediated keratinocyte damage in lichen planus.

questions.q: A 9-year-old girl develops recurrent tender subcutaneous nodules along the lower extremities following episodes of pharyngitis. There is no evidence of systemic involvement after thorough workup. Which infectious agent is most strongly associated with this presentation?
questions.exp: Streptococcal infections are particularly notorious for triggering cutaneous polyarteritis nodosa (cPAN), especially in pediatric patients. Unlike classic PAN where hepatitis B is a major trigger, cPAN in children frequently follows streptococcal pharyngitis.

questions.q: A 52-year-old man presents with fever, weight loss, testicular pain, and palpable purpura on the lower limbs. Laboratory workup reveals elevated inflammatory markers and hepatitis B surface antigen positivity. Mesenteric angiography shows multiple microaneurysms at vessel bifurcations. Which of the following findings would be INCONSISTENT with the diagnosis of classic polyarteritis nodosa?
opts: Necrotizing inflammation of medium-sized muscular arteries
Absence of capillary or venule involvement
questions.exp: Classic polyarteritis nodosa is definitively ANCA-negative, which distinguishes it from small-vessel vasculitides such as microscopic polyangiitis and granulomatosis with polyangiitis. The disease affects medium-sized arteries without involvement of arterioles, capillaries, or venules, and HBV-associated cases demonstrate immune complex deposition.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman with Down syndrome presents with sudden onset of numerous 1-2 mm flesh-colored papules over her anterior chest, neck, and axillae. Histopathology reveals small ductal structures with comma-shaped tails embedded in a dense fibrous stroma. Which histological finding would be MOST concerning for malignant transformation requiring deeper sections and wider excision?
opts: Eosinophilic PAS-positive material within ductal lumina
Two rows of bland cuboidal cells lining the ducts
Deep dermal and subcutaneous infiltration with perineural invasion
questions.exp: Microcystic adnexal carcinoma (MAC) is the malignant counterpart of syringoma and is characterized by deep infiltration into subcutis and perineural invasion, unlike benign syringoma which is confined to superficial dermis. Benign syringomas strictly show NO cytologic atypia and remain superficially located.

questions.q: A 52-year-old woman presents with a 4-month history of violaceous erythema over the eyelids and knuckles without any muscle weakness. Her serum creatine kinase levels are normal, EMG is unremarkable, and MRI of thigh muscles shows no abnormality. Which term best describes her condition?
questions.exp: Amyopathic dermatomyositis is characterized by classic cutaneous manifestations of dermatomyositis with entirely normal muscle enzymes, normal EMG, and normal muscle imaging for at least 6 months. This differs from hypomyopathic DM where subclinical myositis is detectable on investigations despite absence of clinical weakness.

questions.q: A 45-year-old male with lepromatous leprosy presents with gradual visual impairment. Slit-lamp examination reveals thickened corneal nerves with a characteristic 'beads on a string' appearance. Which of the following additional findings would most likely be observed in this patient on further examination?
opts: Loss of eyebrows beginning from the medial third
Superficial punctate keratitis starting in the superior temporal quadrant
questions.exp: Thickened corneal nerves ('beads on a string') are pathognomonic and often the earliest ocular sign of lepromatous leprosy. Miliary lepromas causing superficial punctate keratitis typically start in the superior temporal quadrant in these patients. Eyebrow loss in lepromatous leprosy characteristically begins laterally, not medially.
